purpose: Test whether bounded C++ amplitude-only Rs correction can restore an invalid peak while leaving dendrite length unchanged and synchronization unsettled.

provenance.candidate_source_composition_note: The diagnostic build used the current no-action refusal source from PulseLib cc1160d plus the patch stored beside this record. The root checkout gitlink was older; source hashes and the exact C++ delta are recorded explicitly.

diagnostic_policy.operation: After 3 repeated invalid-peak/low-amplitude/no-action bursts, if Rs remained above Rmin and W3 was off, apply one bounded P-style step to Rs, Rs := clamp(Rs * (1 - 0.15 * gain)); leave length unchanged and reset the no-action counter. At Rmin, retain the explicit refusal.

interpretation: The temporary C++ path avoided the immediate refusal and executed 66 bounded Rs steps, but did not restore a valid peak before the tested Rmin=Rm/10.

For active input 0, the peak was valid at iteration 38 after length growth to 9. It later fell below the peak-validity threshold; the audit does not record the full input sample, so the cause of that transition is unresolved.

During the repeated rescue segment, active-input amplitude rose about 20-fold while Rs fell about 57-fold, but the final peak remained roughly 3.1e5 times below its target and |dt| remained far outside SyncTolerance.

The experiment does not prove that Rs-only recovery is impossible. It shows that this bounded 6% policy did not recover this trajectory within the configured resistance range, and that the no-action refusal was not merely hiding an easy one-step recovery.
The candidate code was used only in an isolated Release build. It was not copied into the production source or committed as trainer behavior.
